title: Project SkyNet Urban Drone Delivery Launch Decision: Financial Investment, Consumer Acceptance, UAM Corridor Compliance, and Fleet.
dek: Analysis of OmniLogistics Corp's Project SkyNet based on internal financial, regulatory, and consumer survey documents.
intro: This report synthesizes three internal documents from OmniLogistics Corp regarding Project SkyNet, an autonomous drone delivery initiative. The documents cover financial investment, regulatory compliance with UAM corridors, and consumer acceptance survey results.
key_takeaways: OmniLogistics is allocating $45.5 million in capital expenditure for Project SkyNet, a 25% increase from initial Q1 projections.
68% of urban residents surveyed are comfortable with drone delivery, but 42% cite noise pollution as a top concern.
The Heavy-Lifter v2 drone exceeds the 25 lbs UAM weight limit by 2.5 lbs, requiring a fleet mix shift to Swift-Class drones.

action_steps.action: Recalibrate fleet mix to prioritize Swift-Class drones (18 lbs) for urban centers to comply with the 25 lbs weight limit.
Deploy Whisper-Prop technology to address noise concerns (42% of respondents) and shutter outward-facing cameras during final descent to address privacy concerns (35%).
Modify dispatch software payload capacity limits as notified to Engineering team.
Ensure flight telemetry and sensor data retention for minimum 90 days as per UAM guidelines.

methodology: Analysis based solely on three internal documents: Q3 Financial Investment Memo (July 18, 2026), Regulatory Update on UAM Corridors (July 10, 2026), and Consumer Acceptance Survey (May-June 2026). No external sources used.
evidence_quality: High. All figures and statements are directly quoted from the provided documents.
disclaimer: This report is generated from the provided private documents only. No external verification has been performed. All facts are as stated in the documents.
